messages.author: fee73ca0c556eec2
messages.subject: Question about mixture modeling
parts:
Hello all Stan users.

I have programmed successfully different parts of the manual. Now I am trying to program the mixture modeling section, but I wonder if it's possible to asses with Stan that problem (mixture of multivariate gaussian) when the number of components in the mixture is unknown. 

Recently I have read a similar problem (conceptually): curve estimation by polynomials of random order, and it was resolved by Jump diffusion sampling and reversible jump algorithm:

http://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0378375897001791

Thank you for your help and this great software.
Angel

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Question about mixture modeling
parts:
We'd love to do more Bayesian non-parametrics directly, but we don't
have any short-term plans to implement variable state-size
sampling. It would require a major rethinking of how sampling
and convergence monitoring and effective sample size measurement
works, for starters.

As the thread Dan pointed to suggests, you can use a large K to
approximate.

- Bob
